subject: Biology
title: The Human Genome
description: A fast breakdown of The Human Genome for builders.

hook.text: The human genome contains about 3.2 billion base pairs of DNA packed into 23 chromosomes.

buildup.text: If you printed the genome as text, it would fill about 200 phone books.

discovery.text: Any two humans share about 99.9% of their DNA. Only 0.1% accounts for all our differences.

twist.text: We share roughly 60% of our genes with bananas and 85% with mice.

climax.text: That tiny fraction of unique DNA shapes everything from eye color to disease risk.

punchline.text: We're 99.9% the same. The 0.1% makes you.

quiz.question: What percentage of DNA do any two humans share?

details.summary: The human genome contains approximately 3.2 billion base pairs encoding about 20,000 protein-coding genes across 23 chromosome pairs. Remarkably, any two humans share about 99.9 percent of their DNA, with the remaining 0.1 percent accounting for all individual variation.
details.whyItMatters: Mapping the human genome revealed that human genetic similarity far exceeds differences. The 0.1 percent of variation that distinguishes individuals holds the keys to personalized medicine, disease susceptibility, and human evolution.
takeaways: The human genome contains 3.2 billion base pairs of DNA
Humans share 99.9 percent of their DNA with each other
Only about 1.5 percent of the genome directly codes for proteins

faq.question: Why do humans have so few genes compared to expectations?
faq.answer: Scientists expected 100,000 or more genes based on human complexity, but found only about 20,000. Complexity arises from how genes are regulated, alternatively spliced into multiple proteins, and interact in networks rather than from sheer gene count.

faq.question: How similar is human DNA to other species?
faq.answer: Humans share about 98.7 percent with chimpanzees, 85 percent with mice, and about 60 percent with bananas. These numbers reflect deep evolutionary conservation of fundamental biological processes shared across all life.
